articles.title: Missile with ‘eyes’: Iran’s new missile can hunt targets without GPS, putting US warships on alert
articles.summary: International News: Iran appears to have used an electro-optical-guided missile against US warships for the first time, marking a potentially significant development in T.
articles.body: Iran appears to have used an electro-optical-guided missile against US warships for the first time, marking a potentially significant development in Tehran’s efforts to threaten American naval forces operating near the Strait of Hormuz. The reported use of the technology comes as Iran has intensified missile attacks on US vessels in recent days.According to The Telegraph, the missiles used in the latest attack were equipped with electro-optical seekers that use cameras and light sensors to identify and track targets. US central command confirmed that Iran launched attacks against American forces and vessels but said all attempted attacks on US warships failed.The strikes came after the US launched retaliatory attacks that destroyed five Iranian oil tankers near Kharg Island, a key Iranian oil hub, escalating the maritime confrontation between Washington and Tehran.Iran had first revealed the new missile system late last year, naming it the Qassem Bassir, a medium-range ballistic missile equipped with electro-optical sensors designed to improve its ability to identify and hit targets.Mohsen Rezaei, Iran's newly installed secretary of the Supreme national security council, meanwhile suggested that a new “special anti-destroyer” missile was used in Wednesday's strike against US ships. However, it remains unclear whether that weapon was the Qassem Basir, meaning the exact missile used in the attack has not been independently confirmed.Iran’s Qassem Bassir missileIran unveiled the Qassem Basir missile in May 2025 as an upgraded version of its Martyr Haj Qassem ballistic missile. According to Iran’s defence ministry, the solid-fuel missile has a range of around 1,200 kilometres and features a manoeuvrable warhead and an upgraded guidance system.Its key feature is an electro-optical guidance system, which Iran says allows the missile to identify targets without relying on GPS and makes it more resistant to electronic jamming.The Qassem Basir is believed to carry a warhead of roughly 500 kilograms, although Iran has not publicly disclosed an official warhead weight. Its 1,200-kilometre range places it in the medium-range ballistic missile category.Strategic implications of electro-optical guidance systemThe electro-optical technology could give Iran a new way to threaten moving US warships by allowing missiles to identify and track targets during the terminal phase while reducing reliance on GPS. Its claimed resistance to electronic jamming could also complicate US efforts to disrupt incoming missiles.The capability could strengthen Iran’s anti-ship and area-denial capabilities around the Strait of Hormuz, potentially increasing the risks for US naval forces operating there. However, its effectiveness would still depend on Iran obtaining accurate targeting data before launch.

articles.title: Fire aboard cargo ship undergoing repairs at busy Chinese port leaves 25 people dead, five more injured
articles.summary: A cargo ship called the Ocean Melody caught fire during repairs at Qingdao port, killing 25 of the 42 people on board the Liberian-flagged vessel.
articles.body: A cargo ship docked for repairs at a port on the northeastern coast of China caught fire Thursday, killing at least 25 people who were on board at the time, according to Chinese state media. The ship was being fixed by Beihai Shipbuilding Co. in the port of Qingdao — one of the country's major shipping hubs — when it caught fire at approximately 11:15 a.m. local time, the Xinhua news agency reported. A total of 42 people were on the vessel at the time of the blaze, and 12 of them were safely rescued, Xinhua reported. Five others were injured and taken to the hospital, where they are in stable condition. CARGO SHIP ATTACKED BY SMALL CRAFT NEAR STRAIT OF HORMUZ, UK MARITIME AGENCY SAYS Photos released by Xinhua identified the ship as the Ocean Melody. The ship-tracking website VesselFinder lists it as sailing under the Liberian flag. The Associated Press reported that the fire was extinguished at around 2:30 p.m., a little over three hours after it started. Videos online showed plumes of white smoke billowing from the ship. The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Chinese authorities have not said what sparked the blaze while the vessel was undergoing repairs. TIM SHEEHY EXPOSES A 'SCARY' SHIPBUILDING COLLAPSE THAT LEAVES THE US VULNERABLE TO CHINA China’s President Xi Jinping called for "intensified efforts" to provide support for those who were affected by the fire, Xinhua reported, adding that Premier Li Qiang said "trapped people" needed to be rescued. Xi also called for ensuring "preventive measures are thoroughly implemented" and "resolutely prevent major and catastrophic accidents." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Beihai Shipbuilding is a subsidiary of the state-owned China State Shipbuilding Corporation, the world's largest shipbuilder. According to the company's website, its primary businesses are shipbuilding and ship repair. Qingdao, in China's Shandong province, is one of the country's busiest ports and a major center for shipbuilding, shipping and international trade. The port handles millions of containers each year and is home to several large shipyards. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Nicolás Maduro’s wife seeks home detention ahead of trial citing ‘serious’ heart condition
articles.summary: The wife of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, Cilia Flores, asked a federal judge late Wednesday to release her from jail pending trial, citing a “serious” heart condition.
articles.body: The wife of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, Cilia Flores, asked a federal judge late Wednesday to release her from jail pending trial, citing a “serious” heart condition. In the filing, Flores’ attorney Mark Donnelly said she “deserves the opportunity to await her trial while on home confinement” in order to recover from a recommended cardiac catheterization, which could lead to more invasive heart procedures. “Prior to the United States’ military invasion of Venezuela, Ms. Flores de Maduro was physically healthy and took no ongoing medication, other than a monthly injection to help control her mitral valve prolapse,” Donnelly said. Now, Flores is prescribed multiple medications, including one to take in the event of a potential heart attack, while continuing to grapple with the medical recommendations that she undergo testing and surgery, he said. Donnelly said Flores has not received her monthly injection for her mitral valve prolapse since her incarceration. Flores, 69, and Maduro, 63, have been held at a Brooklyn jail since U.S. forces captured the couple at their Caracas home in a nighttime raid and brought them to New York to face criminal charges in January. The couple was federally charged with conspiracy to import cocaine, along with possession of machine guns and destructive devices. Maduro is also charged with a narco-terrorism conspiracy. In the indictment, prosecutors in Manhattan alleged that Maduro and his co-conspirators have, “for decades, partnered with some of the most violent and prolific drug traffickers and narco-terrorists in the world, and relied on corrupt officials throughout the region, to distribute tons of cocaine to the United States.” Maduro and Flores have pleaded not guilty to all counts and are scheduled to go to trial in June. They face potential life sentences if a jury finds them guilty. Last week, they asked a federal judge to dismiss the drug trafficking indictment, arguing they are immune from prosecution as the leader and first lady of a foreign country. If Flores were released ahead of trial, her attorney recommended placing her under home detention with GPS location monitoring, 24-hour armed surveillance, surrender of all travel documents, and a third-party custodian approved by pretrial services and the court. Donnelly said the Trump administration is aware of his client’s request but opposes her release. “Despite the ongoing efforts of the MDC staff, a detention center lacks the conditions needed for such a recovery. Her reticence to undergo cardiac exploration and surgery only to return to the conditions which have contributed to the deterioration of her health is reasonable,” he said. Flores has lost more than 25 pounds and two molars and sleeps no more than three to four hours per day, according to Donnelly. On July 29, Flores experienced “a significant, 30-minute episode of intense pressure in her chest along with feeling a lack of oxygen” and “suffers from lingering light-headedness, dizziness, and shortness of breath,” the filing stated. Flores’ legal team, in consultation with outside medical experts, believes she may have suffered a minor heart attack during the July episode. However, because lab tests were not taken or documented in her medical records at the time, the extent of her condition remains unclear, Donnelly said. A spokesperson for the Southern District of New York declined to comment.

articles.title: George W. Bush on 9/11 attacks: The former president on 25th anniversary
articles.summary: Former President George W. Bush recalled how he formulated his first messages to the nation after the Sept.
articles.body: Former President George W. Bush recalled how he formulated his first messages to the nation after the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, saying he didn’t want the country to “lose our soul.” The 43rd president spoke with former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice on Sept. 9 at the George W. Bush Presidential Center in Dallas ahead of the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks. It marks the only public comments Bush plans to make about the anniversary, NBC Dallas-Fort Worth reported, citing his presidential center. Bush and Rice recalled the early moments when they first learned of the attacks in 2001. The former president, who will be appearing at an anniversary event in New York City on Sept. 11, remembered reading to a group of schoolchildren in a classroom in Florida when he was told by an aide that a second plane had hit the World Trade Center in Manhattan. “I didn’t have much time to process that, but it was pretty clear to me that if we were under attack, then my job was to defend the child that was reading to me, and her family, and her country,” Bush said, according to a broadcast of the event by C-SPAN. “And so it was a moment of clarity. “In this case, I became a wartime president,” he continued. “There was no doubt in my mind that this was not a law enforcement event. This was a war, and the job of the president of the country and his team is to rally the nation to do what’s necessary to protect our people.” Rice, 71, was in Washington, D.C., at the time of the attacks and called Bush. “I did something I never would do again,” Rice said. “I raised my voice to you because you said, ‘I’m coming back.’ And I said, ‘Stay where you are. The United States of America is under attack. It’s not safe here.’” Bush flew from Florida to a military base in Louisiana and then one in Nebraska. He chose to fly back to Washington, D.C., despite Rice’s warning, after aides suggested he needed to make a speech to the nation. “I said you’re right I do, but I’m damn sure not going to give it from a bunker in Omaha, Nebraska,” he said. “I thought that would be a psychological victory for those who attacked us. And so I flew back.” Rice and Bush also recalled the frantic moments involving United Airlines Flight 93. The plane was seized by terrorists, who turned the flight toward Washington, D.C. Passengers and crew fought back, and the plane crashed in a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, killing all on board. At first, Rice and Bush said they thought Flight 93 had been shot down. “For about 10 minutes we thought we’d shot down a civilian aircraft,” Rice said. “That always to me represented just how hard the decisions were that you had to (make) under a lot of pressure.” Bush’s mind also turned to what he would tell the nation on Sept. 12. “My main concern was as comforter-in-chief because I had a sense there was a lot of trauma,” he said. “How does one help America have the confidence that we can go forward as a nation?” Rice remembered Bush stressing to her that he wanted the country to regain a sense of normalcy amid flights being grounded, banks being closed and the economy being “totally shut down.” “I didn’t want us to lose our soul,” Bush said. “As we defended our freedoms, I wanted people to remember how precious they are.” Bush also remembered visiting a mosque in the aftermath. “I also made it clear that Islam was a religion of peace, not a religion of war, and that these people subverted their religion,” he said about the terrorists. He also traveled to ground zero in Manhattan to visit with first responders and emergency personnel rushing to help others. “Seeing those firefighters and policemen, it was just unbelievable what they did,” he said. The 25th anniversary of the attacks will be commemorated with solemn ceremonies at ground zero, the Pentagon and Shanksville. There also will be a focus this year on those who have died since the attack from 9/11-related illnesses, including a moment of silence in their memory. Former presidents Bill Clinton, Barack Obama, Joe Biden and Bush are all expected to attend the 9/11 Memorial in Manhattan. President Donald Trump will commemorate the anniversary at the Pentagon in Washington. The names of the more than 3,000 victims will be read aloud as part of the annual ceremony in Manhattan. There also will be moments of silence to mark the exact times when the two planes hit the World Trade Center buildings and when the buildings fell.

articles.title: Bayeux Tapestry unveiled to UK public for first time at British Museum
articles.summary: Visitors tell the BBC it was a "real privilege" to be among the first to see the tapestry in England.
articles.body:
The Bayeux Tapestry has gone on public display in the UK for the first time since it was created nearly 1,000 years ago.

It was originally embroidered in England but kept for centuries in France, and tells the story of the Norman conquest of England and the Battle of Hastings in 1066.

The 70m (230ft)-long 11th Century tapestry is being loaned to the British Museum while its usual home in Normandy, France undergoes renovation.

Doors at the museum opened at 10:00 BST, with shield-wielding re-enactors in costumes from the era waiting outside.

It's a loan almost 100 years in the making, but despite some opposition in France to it being moved, the French Culture minister recently said it arrived in a "wonderful state" .

History buffs arrived early en masse to catch a glimpse of the opening.

Adrian Harris told BBC News that it was a "real privilege" to be one of the first members of the public to see the tapestry in England.

"I'm not a very emotive or expressive person but I was absolutely blown away by it," he said, moments after seeing the tapestry.

He described how he was taken aback when he had an uninterrupted view of it at the top of stairs at the start of the exhibition.

Serena Smith took a tour inside the museum before her slot at 11:30 BST.

When she bought her ticket, she was 4,000th in the queue, despite clicking on a link moments after receiving an email from the British Museum.

"I want you to write that I was first in the queue [today]," she stressed.

Armed with 24 pages of annotated notes, she said she was looking forward to trying to recognise the Normans from their round haircuts, and seeing their boats on board the ships they use to reach the English shores.

Cecilia and Fabio Zanini were completely wowed by the scale of the Bayeux Tapestry.

"I was amazed by the vibrancy of the colours. The detail of the characters," Cecilia said. "It gave both of us goosebumps."

Fabio said he was constantly looking left and right to see all the action and he was surprised by the scale of the tapestry, particularly the number of Norman boats and cavalry.

"It feels like you're in the battlefield," he added, praising the "real sense of movement" in the embroidery.

"It really allowed you to go back to 1066."

But others told the BBC the event was "out of reach" because of its cost and London location.

Angie in Leeds said the "historic event" was "out of reach for many, many families in the north" when you factor in the cost of train tickets and food costs on top of the museum tickets themselves.

"London-only cultural events alienate many families north of Watford," she added.

Another man spoke of the "extreme queuing" required to view the exhibit. Hadyn Blakeston said he felt like he was on a "conveyor belt" while moving along the tapestry.

"It's one long queue," he said. "I know we're supposed to love queuing, but it was extreme queuing."

The tapestry has been inspiring artists since the Middle Ages.

Its July journey from Bayeaux in Normandy to central London - similar to that made across the channel by William of Normandy with his army - was made in the dead of night in a special protective case, to avoid pothole damage, as the BBC's Culture Editor Katie Razzall reported .

The artwork depicts in 58 scenes events leading up to the Battle of Hastings and Norman Conquest of England in 1066.

'Nothing could have prepared me for my first look at the tapestry' - writes BBC Culture editor, Katie Razzall

Razzall said she had been preparing for the exhibition for months.

"I've read books and studied photographs of the tapestry. I was even lucky enough to witness the carefully choreographed unfurling from its case a few days after its arrival from France.

"But nothing prepared me for how I felt when I looked down on it for the first time, stretching the full length of the gallery," she added.

Michael Lewis, one of the four curators for the exhibition, told the Press Association: "1066 is, of course, one of the most important events in English history, and the tapestry is the ultimate reflection of that in terms of a visual narrative.

"Some people see it as akin to a graphic novel or a cartoon or something like that, it's immediately recognisable."

He described France allowing it to come to the UK and be displayed at the British Museum as "an enormous act of diplomacy".

Tickets to the exhibition are sold out until the next release on 21 October.

The Bayeux Tapestry is at the British Museum until 11 July 2027.

articles.title: A North Carolina man paid health insurance for 12 years, missed one payment and lost family coverage; he then canceled a $15,000-$20,000 transfusion
articles.summary: US News: For 12 years, Cord Silverstein paid for health insurance without interruption. Then one missed monthly payment turned into a coverage crisis for his e.
articles.body: For 12 years, Cord Silverstein paid for health insurance without interruption. Then one missed monthly payment turned into a coverage crisis for his entire family and forced him to postpone a medical treatment costing as much as $20,000, states a report by American web portal AOL. The Morrisville, North Carolina, resident believed he had enrolled in automatic payments, but the arrangement failed and after paying his May premium, he missed the June payment. Later, Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina notified him on July 7 that his policy had been canceled, states the report. Six days later, Silverstein contacted the insurer, prepared to settle the outstanding bill. By then, however, reinstatement was no longer an option under the terms of his policy. Scroll down to read what happened next.One missed payment, no easy way backSilverstein was directed to the Health Insurance Marketplace, where he would need to qualify for a special enrollment period to obtain new coverage. But failing to pay an insurance premium does not qualify as a life event that triggers such a period. As a result, he must wait until the next open-enrollment period to purchase a new policy, with coverage not beginning until 2027. The situation highlights a potentially costly distinction in the US health insurance system, a person can lose individual coverage after falling behind on premiums, even after years of uninterrupted payments.Temporary coverage comes with major gapsIn the meantime, Silverstein purchased temporary insurance intended to protect against major emergencies such as hospitalization following an accident or stroke. However, the policy does not cover pre-existing conditions. That became particularly consequential because Silverstein requires a blood transfusion every three months. Paying for the treatment himself would cost approximately $15,000 to $20,000, prompting him to cancel his next scheduled transfusion.Healthcare advocates say cases like this illustrate how complicated insurance rules can create serious financial and medical consequences. Patients may struggle to understand payment deadlines, reinstatement rules, enrollment periods and coverage exclusions, even when they have maintained insurance for years.Grace periods vary by policySilverstein had 25 days after his premium's due date to make the payment. North Carolina law requires a 10-day grace period for individual plans that are not subsidized through a tax credit, according to the state's Department of Insurance. Marketplace customers who receive premium tax credits can have a significantly longer grace period—up to 90 days—provided they have already paid at least one full month's premium during the benefit year. Silverstein did not qualify for the tax credit because his income was too high.His situation was also complicated by the fact that he owns an AI marketing agency and does not receive employer-sponsored insurance. After his insurer stopped accepting credit cards for automatic payments, he moved to manual bank transfers before attempting to automate the payments again.A warning for policyholdersThe experience underscores two practical lessons for people with individual health insurance: confirm that automatic payments are actually active, particularly after an insurer changes its payment systems, and understand exactly how long the policy's grace period lasts.Blue Cross NC says it has processes to notify members when premiums become overdue and warn them about the potential impact on coverage. For consumers, however, Silverstein's experience demonstrates how quickly a routine billing error can become a far more serious healthcare and financial problem.Image Courtesy: istockCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Kuldeep Yadav grabs 10-fer for Yorkshire: Star spinner regains form months before India's busy Test season
articles.summary: Kuldeep Yadav grabbed a sensational 10-wicket match haul for Yorkshire in the County Championship, roaring back to form ahead of India's busy Test season.
articles.body:
Kuldeep Yadav claimed a career-best 10-wicket haul for Yorkshire against Essex, raising his hand ahead of India's busy Test season.

His recent India Test outings against Sri Lanka were poor, with Manav Suthar's two stellar performances making Kuldeep's place uncertain.

Suthar's 10-wicket haul in just his second Test, the best by an Indian bowler in Sri Lanka, has dramatically raised the bar.

Spin wizardry in England! Kuldeep Yadav destroys county attack with 10-fer for Yorkshire ahead of India's Test season

Kuldeep Yadav had a point to prove, and he made it loudly at Headingley as the left-arm wrist spinner tore through Essex's batting lineup across three days.

He produced career-best first-class match figures of 10 for 120 to help Yorkshire romp to an innings and 106-run victory, and in doing so, he delivered a timely reminder of just how dangerous he can be when he's fully firing.

Yorkshire needed this win to cement their place in the County Championship's top flight, and Kuldeep gave them exactly what they needed.

He finished with four for 70 from 20 overs in Essex's first innings, then came back even better in the second, as he claimed six for 50 from 16 overs to wrap things up.

India play two crucial Test series which are part of the ongoing WTC cycle. They tour New Zealand for a two-match series in November, followed by the Border-Gavaskar Trophy where they host Australia for a five-match series in the New Year.

Why does this County performance matter so much for Kuldeep?

The county stint comes at a particularly important moment in Kuldeep's career. His outings in the recent Test series in Sri Lanka were, to put it plainly, underwhelming.

He went wicketless in the first innings of the opening Test while conceding 65 runs from 14 overs; the most expensive spinner in that innings. The second innings brought one wicket at a cost that didn't help his case either.

The second Test brought a different problem as Kuldeep wasn't even in the playing XI, though a BCCI statement clarified the reason was medical rather than purely selection-based.

"Kuldeep Yadav has not fully recovered from his viral illness. He was unavailable for selection in the Playing XI for the second Test against Sri Lanka. However, he can take the field as a concussion substitute, if required," the board confirmed on X.

However, there was much speculation if it was actually a tactical decision to drop him, rather than a medical one.

Manav Suthar's emergence and what it means for Kuldeep

While Kuldeep was struggling, Manav Suthar from Sri Ganganagar produced one of the most stunning performances by an Indian spinner in recent memory.

In only his second Test appearance, Suthar struck with his very first delivery in the first innings, eventually finishing with four for 76 at Galle. He then came back on the final day and tore through Sri Lanka for six for 55, completing a match haul of 10 for 131.

That figure is now the best by an Indian bowler in Sri Lanka, surpassing Harbhajan Singh's 10 for 153 at Galle in 2008 and Ravichandran Ashwin's 10 for 160 at the same ground in 2015.

The equation isn't completely straightforward. Ravindra Jadeja is untouchable in the India Test setup as his all-round value with bat, ball and in the field makes him the first name on the team sheet.

Suthar has now demonstrated he can win Tests on his own, and he offers a batting dimension too with lower-order contributions and that puts Kuldeep in a tight spot.

India's next Test assignment is against New Zealand, where the management may be inclined to go with four pacers, leaving Jadeja as the lone specialist spinner. The Australian series in India that follows later could be where Kuldeep gets his clearest opportunity, as turning pitches at home usually benefit wrist spinners, and his variations become significantly more potent in those conditions.

To remain in contention until January, he must perform at his best in the next four months; consistency will be key for Kuldeep.

The Yorkshire 10-fer is important but not enough on its own

County cricket provides great form and great rhythm, but it doesn't always translate directly into international success, and selectors know that. What Kuldeep needed this match to do is prove he's physically right and mentally reset after a difficult Sri Lanka tour, and in that sense, it does the job.

The real test will come when he's back in an India shirt under pressure, with Suthar's performances still fresh in everyone's memory. Kuldeep is still one of India's most gifted bowlers when everything clicks, as his ability to dismiss top batters with drift and turn is exceptional.

But exceptional talent alone won't keep you in the XI when a younger alternative has just taken 10 wickets in a single Test. The 10-fer at Headingley was a necessary statement. What he does next with it will define the next chapter of his international career.
